lines.japanese: こん、こん……
lines.english: Knock, knock...
Mm...

lines.japanese: こんこん、こん……
lines.english: Knock-knock, knock...
Mm, mmm...

lines.japanese: 意識に入り込んでくる微かな音。なんだろう、なにか隣の家で工事でも……。
lines.english: I started to notice a faint sound. What was it, construction next door or something...?

lines.japanese: こんこんこんこん……
lines.english: Knock-knock-knock-knock...

lines.japanese: あれ、僕の部屋だ。
lines.english: Wait. It was my room.

lines.japanese: 目を開けてみると、時計の針はまだセットした時間にかかってなかった。
lines.english: I opened my eyes. The clock’s hands had not yet reached the time I had set.

lines.japanese: 音のする方向を目で辿ってみると、部屋の入り口から小さな音が断続的に聞こえてくる。
lines.english: I followed the sound to the entrance of my room, where it came and went in faint bursts.

lines.japanese: 思わず首を捻った。叔父さんと叔母さんの居ないこの家で、僕以外にこの部屋の戸を叩けるのは一人しかいない。
lines.english: I tilted my head. With my uncle and aunt away, there was only one person besides me who could knock on this door.

lines.japanese: 「……おはよう？」
lines.english: “...Good morning?”

lines.japanese: 何故か疑問系。襖を開くと、僕の妹が空中を叩いていた。
lines.english: For some reason, it came out as a question. When I slid the door open, my sister was knocking on empty air.

lines.japanese: 「おはよ」
lines.english: “Morning.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は手の動きがくせになったみたいだ。しばらくなにもない空中をノックしていた。
lines.english: The motion seemed to have become a habit. For a little while longer, she kept knocking on nothing.

lines.japanese: 「お、おはよ」
lines.english: “G-good morning.”

lines.japanese: 「どうしたの？」
lines.english: “What is it?”

lines.japanese: もしかして、僕のことを起こしに来てくれたんだろうか。いや、まさか。そんなこと今までになかったじゃないか。
lines.english: Could she have come to wake me? No, surely not. She had never done anything like that before.

lines.japanese: 「あれ？」
lines.english: “Hm?”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Mm-hm?”

lines.japanese: 「ごはん、できてるから」
lines.english: “Breakfast is ready.”

lines.japanese: 彼女はそれだけを告げると、ぱたぱたと階段を駆けおりていった。なんだろう、まさかほんとに起こしに来てくれたのかな。
lines.english: She said just that, then pattered down the stairs. What was that? Had she really come just to wake me?

lines.japanese: そんなの漫画の中だけの出来事だと思ってた。我がことながら不思議な感じだ。
lines.english: I thought things like that happened only in manga. It felt strange to experience it myself.

lines.japanese: うわっ！
lines.english: Whoa!

lines.japanese: 背中から大きな音が鳴りはじめた。今度こそ僕の予定起床時刻になったみたいだ。
lines.english: A loud noise started behind me. Looked like my alarm was finally going off.

lines.japanese: 着替えて洗面所で顔を洗いながら、なんとなく考えた。
lines.english: After changing, I washed my face and found myself wondering.

lines.japanese: なんだろう、体が軽い。朝って基本的にだるいものじゃなかったっけ。
lines.english: What was this? I felt light. Weren't mornings usually supposed to make you feel sluggish?

lines.japanese: 昨日は走ったり驚いたり、とにかく忙しい一日だった。疲れていてもいいはずなんだけどな。
lines.english: Yesterday I'd run around, gotten startled, and just generally had a busy day. I should've been tired.

lines.japanese: それにしても色んな出来事がいっぺんに起こった日だった。もしかしたら、僕の三年間分の思い出よりも中身が凝縮された一日だったんじゃないか。
lines.english: Still, that was a day when all kinds of things happened at once. Maybe it had more packed into it than all my memories from the past three years.

lines.japanese: 今日から山科さんも作業に加わってくれるし、作業の量は多いけどやりがいがある。
lines.english: Yamashina would join our work today. There was a great deal to do, but it felt worthwhile.

lines.japanese: 僕はタオルで水気を拭うと、妹が準備を済ませてくれているはずの食卓へ向かった。
lines.english: I dried my face with a towel and went to the table, where my sister should have finished laying out breakfast.

lines.japanese: もぐもぐ。
lines.english: Munch, munch.

lines.japanese: 目の前でも、もぐもぐ。
lines.english: Across from me: munch, munch.

lines.japanese: 今朝はパン食だった。例のパン屋さんで買った、ちょっといいパンだ。
lines.english: Breakfast was bread today—the slightly nicer kind from that bakery.

lines.japanese: 生野菜と目玉焼きが乗ったお皿の横に、マーガリンやジャムが並んでいる。
lines.english: Margarine and jam sat beside the plates of raw vegetables and fried eggs.

lines.japanese: 「今日はいちごジャムでもつけようかな……はは」
lines.english: “Maybe I’ll have strawberry jam today... Haha.”

lines.japanese: 僕は明るい色のビンを手にとって妹に見せた。特に返事はなかったけど、小さくこくんとうなずいた気がする。
lines.english: I picked up the brightly colored jar and showed it to my sister. She did not answer, but I thought I saw a tiny nod.

lines.japanese: 朝から甘い味を口にするのは眠気も招きそうな気もするけど、たまには試してみるのもいい。僕はスプーンの裏側でジャムをすくうと、パンの表面に撫でつけていった。
lines.english: Eating something sweet first thing in the morning might make me sleepy, but it couldn't hurt once in a while. I scooped up some jam with the back of my spoon and smoothed it over the bread.

lines.japanese: もぐもぐ。
lines.english: Munch, munch.

lines.japanese: うーん、今日はなんの会話をしようかな。
lines.english: Hmm. What should we talk about today?

lines.japanese: 色んな話題はあるんだけど、小鳩の興味を引けそうな話っていうと難しいな。
lines.english: I had plenty to talk about, but coming up with something Kobato might be interested in was tough.

lines.japanese: オンラインの話、インディーズバンドの話があるけど、どれも目の前の行儀いい妹には似合わない話題のような気がする。
lines.english: I could talk about online stuff or indie bands, but none of that seemed right for my well-behaved little sister sitting across from me.

lines.japanese: うーん、なにかないかな、なにか……。
lines.english: Hmm. There had to be something, something...

lines.japanese: うーん、なにか……ん？
lines.english: Hmm. Something... Hm?

lines.japanese: あれ、今なにか聞こえたような？
lines.english: Wait. Had I just heard something?

lines.japanese: 「あれ？　いま何か……ごめん、よく聞き取れなくて」
lines.english: “Sorry, did you say something? I couldn’t quite hear.”

lines.japanese: 「……ご、ごめん」
lines.english: “...S-sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　あ、いや、いいよ。おれもちょっと考えごとしてたからさ」
lines.english: “What? No, it’s all right. I was lost in thought too.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そじゃなくて、昨日のこと」
lines.english: “N-not that. About yesterday.”

lines.japanese: 「昨日？」
lines.english: “Yesterday?”

lines.japanese: 昨日って、なにか謝られるようなことあったかなあ。
lines.english: Did anything happen yesterday that she'd need to apologize for?

lines.japanese: 「昨日、渡来さんって女のひとから、あの、何度か電話があって」
lines.english: “Yesterday, a woman named Watarai called several times, and...”

lines.japanese: 「ああ」
lines.english: “Oh.”

lines.japanese: そういえば、渡来さんも小鳩が電話に出たって言ってたっけ。そっか、そうだった。
lines.english: Watarai had said Kobato answered the phone. Of course. I remembered now.

lines.japanese: 「つた、伝えわすれちゃって、ごめん」
lines.english: “I f-forgot to tell you. Sorry.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩はパンを咥えながら、面目なさそうに顔を伏せた。
lines.english: With bread still between her lips, Kobato lowered her face, looking ashamed of herself.

lines.japanese: 「そのことなら大丈夫だよ。そのあと、ちゃんと電話があったんだ」
lines.english: “That’s all right. She called again afterward, and we spoke.”

lines.japanese: 「うん……うんっ」
lines.english: “Yes... yes.”

lines.japanese: 「あれ？　知ってた？」
lines.english: “Hm? Did you know?”

lines.japanese: 「部屋のまえ通ったら、話しごえ聞こえたから……」
lines.english: “I passed your room and heard you talking...”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんだ」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: 何時ごろだろう、僕は話に夢中で気がつかなかったみたいだ。
lines.english: What time was that? I guess I was too caught up in the conversation to notice.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、知らせに来てくれたんだね。ありがとう」
lines.english: “So you came to let me know. Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、今日はごはん……いる？」
lines.english: Um, do you... want dinner today?

lines.japanese: 「うん、今日はいつも通りお願いするよ」
lines.english: “Yeah. The usual, please.”

lines.japanese: 「うんっ」
lines.english: “Okay.”

lines.japanese: こくん。
lines.english: A tiny nod.

lines.japanese: 普通の人から見たらその動きは小さいかもしれないけど、彼女にしては大きくうなずいた。いつもありがとう。
lines.english: It might've looked like a small movement to anyone else, but for her it was a big nod. Thanks, as always.

lines.japanese: うん、今日は会話らしい会話が出来たんじゃないかな。渡来さんからの電話っていう飛び道具があったけど、それでも会話になったことは確かだ。
lines.english: Yeah, I think we actually managed something like a real conversation today. Granted, Watarai's phone call helped me out, but it was still a conversation.

lines.japanese: 僕はジャムを乗せたパンの最後のひとかけを口に放りこんだ。
lines.english: I put the last morsel of jam-covered bread into my mouth.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、お先に」
lines.english: “I’ll go on ahead, then.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あの」

lines.english: “Hm?”

lines.japanese: 立ちあがろうとしたら、俯いたままの小鳩に待ったをかけられた。
lines.english: I had started to rise when Kobato, still looking down, stopped me.

lines.japanese: 「どしたの？」
lines.english: “What is it?”
“Well...”

lines.japanese: 「えっと……」
髪に隠れて見えにくかったけど、小鳩の目が左右にきょろきょろと動いたように見える。僕は黙って彼女の言葉の続きを待った。
lines.english: Her hair made it hard to see, but I thought her eyes darted from side to side. I waited silently for her to continue.

lines.japanese: 「最近、楽しそうだね」
lines.english: “You seem happy lately.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 意外な言葉だった。小鳩にはそう見えるんだろうか。
lines.english: The words were unexpected. Was that how I looked to Kobato?

lines.japanese: どうなんだろう。僕はなんて答えればいいのか分からずに、ちょっと首を傾げた。
lines.english: I wasn't sure. I didn't know what to say, so I tilted my head a little.

lines.japanese: 「そうかな。うんまあ、普通だよ」
lines.english: “Do I? Well, I’m pretty normal.”

lines.japanese: とりあえずそう答えておいた。というよりも、それしか答えようがない。
lines.english: For now, that was what I said. Or rather, it was the only thing I could say.

lines.japanese: うん、そうだ。なにも特別な一日ってわけじゃない。普通、普通。
lines.english: Yes. That was right. There was nothing particularly special about today. Normal. Perfectly normal.

lines.japanese: 「うん、そか」
lines.english: “Okay. I see.”

lines.japanese: 「うんうん」
lines.english: “Mm-hm.”

lines.japanese: 「そか、そだね」
lines.english: “I see. Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「それだけ？」
lines.english: “Was that all?”

lines.japanese: 小鳩がこくんと頷いたので、僕は浮いた腰を起こしてそのまま台所へと向かった。
lines.english: Kobato gave a tiny nod, so I rose the rest of the way and headed into the kitchen.

lines.japanese: そっか、楽しそうに見えるんだ。うん、それはきっといいことだ。
lines.english: So I looked happy. Yes. Surely that was a good thing.

lines.japanese: ちょっと振りかえると、居間に座る小鳩の肩はなんだか小さく見えた。
lines.english: I glanced back. Kobato sat in the living room, and somehow her shoulders looked small.
